rounds.text: GIC Housing Finance Ltd is profoundly under-appreciated, trading at a steep discount with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.38x against a book value of ₹ 391 per share, while the market price sits at ₹ 148 [E2]. This massive undervaluation is highlighted by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 564 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 73.7% [E39, E40]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price absurdly prices in a -11.3% earnings contraction, contrasting sharply with actual improving momentum like a 54% year-on-year net profit surge and accelerating earnings growth [E41, E61, E64]. The company also rewards patient holders with a solid dividend yield of 3.04% [E4], supported by a supportive financial services sector tailwind [E68]. Conceded: the company has delivered poor long-term sales growth and negative operating cash flow of ₹ -320 Cr in March 2026 [E15, E31]. Yet, fundamentals are outpacing the depressed stock price, with capital expenditure build-up via rising CWIP signaling active growth efforts underneath stale market sentiment [E34, E50, E69].
